summary.intent: Work through the Callisto NEXT-WORK plan in parallel lanes (release retry fix, test debt, docs refresh, init/derive refactors, SYS-NAPI, guard hardening), then pivot to a performance investigation: benchmark the CLI, batch/bulk git operations, evaluate gix and other libraries, and profile where time goes.
summary.outcome: Closed the mistaken plan PR #201 and kept the plan local; opened PRs #202-#208 (SYS-RETRY fix, mixed-routing test, docs refresh, init test/template moves, SYS-NAPI, derive split), hardening PRs #325/#326, and a stacked perf series (#327 benchmark, #328 bulk reads, #330 single-pass history). Status at 200 packages went from ~2 s/405 git processes to ~78 ms/6, and the history redesign was committed and pushed to #330 after CI passed.

repo: Tracking and handoff plans such as NEXT-WORK.md must stay local (.claude/plans/, excluded via .git/info/exclude), never in a commit or PR.
`just ci` must be judged by the log's own `exit=` line, not the background wrapper's exit code; the task notification only reports that the script exited.
AGENTS.md forbids session links in commits/PRs, and reversing an ADR (e.g. ADR 5 system-git-only) needs a new owner-accepted ADR.

ADR 5 removed gix because two backends diverged (gix ignored TagSignPolicy), it added 106 crates, and the CLI needed the git binary anyway; ADR 6 dropped WASM because gix object reads panic under WASI mmap.

Release test harness fakes cargo/gh/registry, so fakes can hide bugs; tests should use the real tool where possible. The harness has set_registry_unreachable but cannot make a registry fail once and then recover.
Fixtures that tag every package on one commit hide per-package git log cost; a realistic independent-versioning fixture revealed 11.7 s status at 500 packages vs the apparent 6 git processes.

Sandbox/guard rejects inline env commands, heredocs, and compound commands mentioning git, so scripts are written to files and run separately; edits are only permitted inside the current worktree; macOS bash lacks mapfile and BSD sed rejects some one-liners.
Test fakes that answer `git tag --list` make switching the tag index to a single for-each-ref call a wide change.

code.finding: Release selection previously treated a tag at HEAD as 'released'; SYS-RETRY fix now observes all operations for packages tagged at HEAD before deciding. A private cat-file --batch reader here was moved to a shared git_batch module.
Git failure in change inference is downgraded to a warning under a borrowed diagnostic code, so the package is silently not bumped.
Subprocess runner sleeps 50 ms after the first poll, imposing a 50 ms floor on every git call.

Change detection now uses a single git log pass; correct semantics for tags are commits reachable from HEAD xor the tag (symmetric difference), matching the old per-tag walk including unmerged hotfix tags.

workflow: Write the failing reproduction first, and mutate the source to prove new tests can fail (done for the mixed-routing and derive snapshot tests).
For pure refactors, commit characterization/snapshot tests first on unchanged code, then do the move so snapshots pass unchanged.
Measure before adding dependencies; the benchmark corrected earlier estimates (retracted a claimed 5x commit-hash batch speedup, measured ~25%).
Use a separate target directory for profiling builds so they don't contend with CI's cargo lock; timings are noisy when another process compiles.
Stack dependent PRs with the native gh stack linking (#207, #329).

friction: Plan file was initially published as PR #201 against the user's intent, requiring a closure and an apology.
Plan path in the original lane summary was wrong and the plan file could not be updated from a background session in the shared checkout.
Several CI runs failed late (stray blank line, lint on complex return type, init tests relying on tag-at-HEAD premise, uncommitted package refused), costing full gate re-runs.
Sandbox restrictions on heredocs, inline env, and git-mentioning scripts forced many temp script files.
My first profile was misleading and earlier performance claims (6 git processes) were fixture artifacts, requiring retractions.
Benchmark timings were noisy because another process was compiling.
open_items: PR #202 review findings (multi-paragraph tag rejection, dependent tagged at HEAD with untagged dependency) were being addressed; no independent review result recorded as merged.
#204 still lists SYS-RETRY/T08-RETRY and needs a follow-up edit after #202 merges.
W0 branch deletion (about 35 local branches plus docs/next-work-plan, docs/spec-rewrite, fix/native-resolution) awaits the user's per-branch call; docs/next-work-plan branch/worktree remains.
W1 real-service credential check needs a decision on where it runs in CI; D01 blocks SYS-MATURIN and W9; W10 needs two decisions; W11 needs credentials.
#326 does not enforce the A2 check at executor adoption; fail-closed registry path is only covered by code reading.
Unmerged stack bug (#323/#324): npm confirmation window restarts per publish and counts only sleep time, so it can be unbounded; to fix.

Credential-hardening PR for version.rs raw git stderr (7 sites), silent inference failures, 0.0.0-alpha snapshot misdetection, and the __CALLISTO_TEST_SLEEP_SCALE production-path hazard are not yet fixed.
Structural audit items (digest from enum order, pre.json version, public fields on validated types, dead public API, license-boundary recipe) need user approval.

Perf follow-ups: commit-hash manifest batch plus single tag listing, a git-time column in the benchmark, CPU profile of non-git time, parallel manifest parsing/directory walk, mimalloc on musl, bounded thread pool for preflight, moving trust re-check (needs sign-off), release-pr decide running full status(), gix read-only experiment (needs new ADR), a CI benchmark threshold.
